subject.title: [Bug]: GitHub Copilot anthropic-messages transport silently hangs ~365s in isolated cron sessions (2026.5.27)

question: After live current-main Copilot Claude cron proof, should aborted/no-output Copilot runs enter model fallback, or should OpenClaw rely on the 60-second idle-timeout path plus cron error status without retrying fallback?
rationale: The code can identify the remaining bypass, but the correct behavior affects side-effect safety and user expectations for cron retries after an indeterminate model run.

options.title: Prove then add narrow fallback
options.body: Run a live Copilot Claude isolated-cron proof first, then allow fallback only for side-effect-safe aborted/no-output results with tests documenting the retry boundary.

options.title: Keep aborts terminal
options.body: Treat aborted/no-output Copilot runs as terminal errors and improve diagnostics rather than risking repeated side effects through fallback.

options.title: Broaden fallback immediately
options.body: Let aborted/no-output results use the configured fallback path now, accepting the risk that some cron tasks may partially repeat work.

recommendation.title: Prove then add narrow fallback
recommendation.body: Run a live Copilot Claude isolated-cron proof first, then allow fallback only for side-effect-safe aborted/no-output results with tests documenting the retry boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice crosses GitHub Copilot routing, stream behavior, and the cloud idle-timeout mitigation history associated with this area.
